newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans slip on rumors Brazil strike averted.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans slip on rumors Brazil strike averted.

text.p: CBOT nearby soybean futures were weaker, with the May and July contracts in fast dealings, amid rumors a strike at Brazil's Paranagua port had been averted, traders said.
But Brazilian sources told Reuters there was no confirmation the strike had been averted.
Port directors and union leadership were meeting at 1230 CST.
The port spokeswoman said there probably would be no word on a resolution before 1800 local/1500 CST.
Dockworkers are asking for a 21 percent pay increase which they say they are owed since last year. The strike was called for Wednesday.

Port sources said a strike would have little effect on soybean exports because they are loaded by automated conveyor belts. A spokeswoman said the export terminal can be operated by only five employees.
At 1239 CST, soybeans were down 2-1/2 cents to up 3-1/4 cents, with March off 2-1/2 at $8.02-1/2 a bushel.
